rationale: The book's core identification of righteousness as right-living (God as its definitional measure; for those under authority, the doing of His commandments as the law kept and worn) best unifies the supplied texts without contradiction. It accounts for the explicit OT equations of commandments with righteousness, the doer-is-righteous test, the servant-duty exclusion of wage claims, the gift/reckoning language of Romans 4 and Philippians 3, and the garment of righteous acts, while prior findings on works, works of the law, faith, belief, and love supply the consistent vocabulary that prevents reading the gift as a re-labeling of wrong-living. The common forensic-status reading explains status language well but under-explains or requires extra steps for the active/doer texts and the explicit commandment identifications; the book therefore carries the full entry as the superior overall account.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is right-living: God is right-living by definition (His ways and works the measure); for those under His authority it is the doing of His commandments (the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts). It is given and reckoned by grace, yet the gift never renames wrong-living right; complete obedience earns no wage because the servant has only done his duty.
book_secondary_elaborations: Garment/armor imagery as the visible wearing of the righteous acts (fine linen = dikaiōmata; breastplate of righteousness as God's own war-dress lent to the soldier)

Dependence on the prior definitions of love (covenant allegiance in commandment-keeping), knowing, faith (trusting faithfulness through obedience), and belief (receiving the word as governing truth that submits)
Paul's wage/debt vocabulary carefully limited to the laborer claiming payment (Rom 4), not to obedience itself (Luke 17:7-10)
Distinction that works are deeds that become obedience only when they execute a legitimate command
Rejection of any reading that flattens 'not of works' into abolition of the law's definition of right-living
strongest_counter_interpretation: The dominant common interpretation: righteousness primarily signifies right standing before God (a forensic/relational status of being declared or credited righteous through faith in Christ, often pictured as an imputed garment or robe covering the sinner), rather than righteousness achieved by human works or primarily identified with ongoing commandment-keeping.
counter_core_identification: Righteousness as right standing/status before God (imputed or conferred by grace through faith, apart from works of the law), with ethical conformity or deeds as secondary fruit or evidence rather than the primary referent.
material_core_denial: The counter treats the primary referent as a conferred status that can be possessed independently of the doing of righteousness; the book insists the referent is the right-living itself (doer is righteous), so that status language never re-labels wrong-living as right.
counter_case: Genesis 15:6 / Romans 4:3-8: faith 'counted/credited/imputed' as righteousness and 'without works,' with David’s blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness and will not impute sin, favoring a forensic declaration.

Romans 3:21-26 / Philippians 3:9 / 2 Corinthians 5:21: righteousness of God through faith in Christ, 'not having a righteousness of my own from the law,' and becoming the righteousness of God in him, read as status conferred apart from personal law-keeping.
Isaiah 61:10 / Ephesians 6:14 garment and breastplate imagery traditionally taken as covering/protection of status rather than fabric woven of the wearer’s own righteous acts.
The Protestant forensic tradition’s long reading of these texts as justification by imputed righteousness, with ethical living as consequent sanctification rather than the definition of the term.
book_explanatory_advantages: Directly equates commandments with righteousness in the supplied texts (Deut 6:25; Ps 119:172) without needing to relegate them to a secondary sense.
Takes 1 John 3:7 ('he that doeth righteousness is righteous') at face value as definitional rather than merely evidential.
Integrates Luke 17:7-10 and Romans 4:4-5 into one coherent wage-vs-duty distinction, so grace reckoning never becomes permission to rename disobedience as righteousness.
Unifies the garment texts (Rev 19:8 dikaiōmata as righteous acts given and worn; Isaiah 61:10) with the commandment equations and the doer test.

Remains consistent with the already-accepted prior findings on works (deeds, not synonym for obedience), works of the law (context-specific denial of purchase-price claims), faith, belief, and love (all converging on commandment-keeping response).
Preserves God’s own righteousness as definitional right-living (Deut 32:4; Ps 145:17) without forcing a purely forensic reading onto the divine subject.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Accounts cleanly for the forensic vocabulary of counting/imputing and the exclusion of wage-works in Romans 4.
Explains the sharp contrast in Philippians 3:9 between 'my own righteousness, which is of the law' and 'the righteousness which is of God by faith' as status transfer.
Matches the traditional Protestant emphasis on justification as declared standing that covers the sinner, using the robe imagery as covering rather than woven deeds.
Avoids any appearance of making personal obedience the ground of right standing before God.
decisive_sources: Deuteronomy 6:25 and Psalm 119:172 (explicit equation of doing the commandments with righteousness)
Luke 17:7-10 together with Romans 4:4-8 (duty vs. wage claim, preserving grace reckoning without renaming wrong-living)
Philippians 3:9 (righteousness of God by faith, read against the book’s wage/debt and prior works findings rather than as pure status independent of right-living)
Revelation 19:8 (fine linen = righteous acts of the saints, given and worn) as developed in the garments chapter
Deuteronomy 32:4 and Psalm 145:17 (God as definitionally right in His ways and works)
Prior FULL findings on works, works of the law, faith, belief, and love that supply the consistent grammar for the book’s distinctions
unresolved_objections: Some forensic-status language (especially the traditional Protestant reading of imputation in Romans 4 and 2 Corinthians 5:21) retains residual force and is not exhaustively re-parsed by every tradition; the book’s integration is superior overall but does not erase every historical confessional difference on mechanism.

The precise scope of which commandments constitute the 'righteous acts' for every covenant member in every age is not fully settled by the supplied entry alone (though the core definition does not require it).
